messages:
Kiran: quick post-GA huddle  we need a crisp rule for tiny customer asks vs roadmap bets. Two customers pinged about search ordering tweak.
Anya: propose: if <=3 dev-days and affects >1 paying customer -> fast lane. Otherwise backlog grooming.
Ben: add caveat: any change touching runtime/model outputs requires an eval gate and canary. Even small changes can shift embed distances.
Pat: operationally, assign 1 engineer from stability lane and 1 from velocity lane and cap scope to 3 story points. If it grows, escalate to mini-epic.
Maria: acceptance criteria for fast fixes: repro steps, automated unit/regression test, 24h canary with monitoring dashboard, rollback playbook.
Kiran: CS note: we have 2 paid customers asking for reorder; theyd accept a 2-day turn.
cs-bot: created ticket #CS-811 with customer details at 2024-11-18T14:22:00Z
Anya: decision: treat as fast-lane small fix. Ben to spike risk profile today, Pat to allocate pair tomorrow morning.
Ben: risk spike: if we change post-processing ranking, run A/B on top-5 order retention and measure click-through delta on canary.
Pat: will add `cs-priority` tag and schedule a quick groom. If spike shows model drift >0.2% top-10, we stop and scope mini-epic.
Kiran: timeline check: aim to ship patch mid-week, with CS quick note explaining temporary workaround (route pin) if any regressions.
Maria: summary: fast-lane approved under strict eval gates and 24h canary. Any broader perf/runtime work stays in next sprint planning.
Anya: I'll update the post-GA playbook and add the fast-lane checklist.
summary: Approved a fast-lane for a small customer-facing search ordering fix: criteria <=3 dev-days, >1 paying customer, eval gates + 24h canary, rollback playbook. Owners assigned and CS notified.
